clue.text: Mixed drink for eponymous hero

definitions.meaning: beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub drink
Tristram, the title character of Laurence Sterne's eighteenth-century comic novel

explanation.surface: A cocktail is named after the hero of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: A hero is eponymous when the work is named after him; Sterne's novel is The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a beer-and-lemonade blend and Sterne's title character, so each half is a separate sense.

clue.text: Weapons not used at the front?

definitions.text: Weapons not used at the front?

parts.words: Weapons not used at the front?
parts.note: pistols worn on the hip are carried at a soldier's flank rather than at the front line, and the question mark flags the literal reading

explanation.definitionFit: Pistols or swords worn at the belt are weapons carried on the flank, hence the name.

clue.text: Taking a short time to get excited, mostly?

definitions.text: Taking a short time to get excited, mostly?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a brief while

indicators.note: most of the word but not all, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or excite

explanation.surface: Someone who warms up quickly, with a question about how fast they get worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ROUSE to ROUS. Read as a whole, someone who takes very little time to get aroused is the answer, which is why the clue ends with a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover who is quickly aroused is passionate and fond of lovemaking.

clue.text: Source of consumer advice to pass on to artist

parts.note: to pass on is a euphemism for to die
Titian, the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A consumer-rights adviser is handing a tip to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' is literal: the advice is about what people eat, not about shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition professional advises people who consume food on what they should eat.

clue.text: Frequently ring a couple of newspapers

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
the FT is the Financial Times, one British daily paper
The Times, another British daily paper, the one this puzzle appeared in

explanation.surface: Someone regularly telephones two newspaper offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a verb (to telephone) but supplies a round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning often, many a time.

clue.text: European in plane or legendary ship

definitions.meaning: a man from the Netherlands travelling by air, read literally
the phantom vessel of sailors' folklore, doomed to sail forever

explanation.surface: A traveller from the Continent is either on a flight or aboard a mythical vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an airborne man from Holland, and also the ghost ship of legend that Wagner made an opera of.

clue.text: Short fellow acting in title role

parts.note: Tim is the short form of the man's name Timothy
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A small man is performing the lead part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' suggests a small man, but it means a shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is named after its leading character, so he is the play's name part.

clue.text: Record times

definitions.meaning: the official written account of a meeting
small units of time, sixty seconds each

explanation.surface: Someone notes down timings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is both the written account of a meeting and the plural of a sixty-second unit.

clue.text: Band's tour in Home Counties

indicators.note: the word tour sits within the letters for Home Counties

parts.note: the counties round London lie in the South East, abbreviated SE
a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: A pop group is playing a series of dates around London's commuter belt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London; 'Band' looks like a music group but is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow strip of colour, a band across a surface.

clue.text: Novel male combination

definitions.meaning: the 1862 Russian novel by Ivan Turgenev
a pairing of men from two generations of one family

explanation.surface: A new way of putting men together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Turgenev's book takes its title from the two generations it portrays, a male parent-and-offspring pairing.

clue.text: Desert animal roamed freely in arid surroundings

indicators.note: the scrambled word sits in the arid word
the arid word forms the surroundings for the scrambled letters

parts.note: arid means dry

indicators.note: the letters of roamed move about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A camel wandered at will across the dry wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' makes OMEDAR from the fodder; 'in ... surroundings' says the dry word encloses it. 'Desert' is the place, not the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-humped camel is the classic beast of the Arabian sands.

clue.text: Youth clubs may be so described

definitions.meaning: a young person below the age of legal adulthood
in bridge, clubs and diamonds are the lower-ranking suits

explanation.surface: Clubs for young people have a particular label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth clubs' reads as one phrase (social clubs for teenagers) but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A person under age is a juvenile, and in bridge clubs are one of the two lower-ranking suits.

clue.text: Cancel a trip round Circle Line

indicators.note: the a-and-trip pair goes round the other letters

parts.note: a bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder, a trip-up
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone calls off a journey on London Underground's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it splits into O and L. 'trip' is a slip, BISH in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To do away with a law or custom is to cancel it entirely.

clue.text: No partners come first all the time =

parts.note: North and South are partners at the bridge table
to top is to come first, head a list

explanation.surface: Without a partner, someone always comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as a pair against East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes on without stopping continues all the time.

clue.text: Kenyan entering mile, since extremely fit

parts.note: as can mean since, because
A1 means first-class, in excellent condition, here written with the letter I for the figure 1

explanation.surface: A Kenyan athlete runs the mile, being supremely fit.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenyans are famous middle-distance runners, so 'mile' fits the athletic picture; A1 (first-rate) stands as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: The people are a nomadic pastoral group of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Medical group appearing hot and bothered

parts.note: red-hot; red is the colour of heat
cross means annoyed, bothered

explanation.surface: Doctors look flushed and flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot and bothered' reads as one idiom but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The international humanitarian organisation gives medical aid in wars and disasters.

clue.text: Take a stone, since it's pronounced fine cheese

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a stone is a rock, since is for, and it's is read as it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take a pebble because it is a cheese of note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' is the sound signal: 'rock for it' said aloud gives the cheese's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A French blue cheese from sheep's milk, matured in caves, is a famous fine cheese.

clue.text: Poet's composed sonnet about city

indicators.note: the rearranged word wraps around the city
the letters of sonnet are composed into a new arrangement

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: A poet has written a fourteen-line poem about a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges SONNET into TENSON, which goes about NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Blue joined county players

parts.note: Down is a county in Northern Ireland
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: Someone is sad after signing for a county team.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland; 'players' suggests sport but means actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means sad, and so does being dejected.

clue.text: Instrument used in no car in ages

indicators.note: the letters are used within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something has not been played in a car for years.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument is in the letters of 'nO CAR IN Ages'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Signal sounded for people waiting

indicators.note: the word for signal is spoken and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: a cue is a signal to begin

explanation.surface: A bell rings to call those standing in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounded' looks like ringing a signal but is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of people waiting their turn.

clue.text: Selfishness can make one run away from disease

indicators.note: the run leaves the disease word

parts.note: ergotism is poisoning from eating grain infected with ergot fungus
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a single run

explanation.surface: Self-absorption can cause one to flee from illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from ERGOTISM leaves the answer; 'run away' looks like fleeing but splits into the piece and the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive self-regard and putting oneself first is a form of selfishness.

clue.text: Casual piece of work in curious book

parts.note: odd means curious, strange
Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A temporary task appears in a strange book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is the Book of Job.
explanation.definitionFit: A small one-off task, done casually, as by a handyman.

clue.text: No girl turns to dunderhead as one of her best friends

indicators.note: the words no and girl are turned to read backwards

parts.note: maid is an old word for a girl
the head, or first letter, of dunder

explanation.surface: Rather than date a fool, a girl turns to her best friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses NOMAID into DIAMON. The definition draws on the song line that diamonds are a girl's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The song from Gentlemen Prefer Blondes calls these gems a girl's best friend.

clue.text: Firm set up a little group of milkmaids, for example

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: A company assembles a small team of dairy workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol The Twelve Days of Christmas has eight maids a-milking, so the milkmaids are an example of a set of eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eight things, like the eight maids a-milking in the carol.

clue.text: One who'd organised a dance

indicators.note: the letters are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: Somebody arranged a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges ONE and WHOD (the apostrophe drops out).
explanation.definitionFit: A lively American folk dance, or the party where it is danced.

clue.text: Shared drug

definitions.meaning: held or done in common, as a shared account

explanation.surface: Narcotics passed around.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means held in common, and also a rolled cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: Following old god, the right places to pray in

indicators.note: the right-wing party comes after the old god

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
the Tories are the right-wing British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Followers of an old god have the right places to worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' sets the party after the old god. 'the right' is the political right, not correctness, and the Tories are Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Small chapels for private prayer are places of worship.

clue.text: To flourish in tragedy is hard

parts.note: Brand is a tragic verse drama by Henrik Ibsen
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Thriving in a tragedy is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragedy' is the title of one: Ibsen's Brand.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave a weapon about showily is to flourish it.

clue.text: Detail of flower in composition of Manet's

indicators.note: the letters of Manet's are put into a new composition

parts.note: the painter's name with its s, used as letters

explanation.surface: A small part of a flower appears in one of Manet's paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' suggests a painting by Manet, but signals an anagram of MANETS.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing male organ is a small part of a flower.
